I farm 12 mu, and with some family labor going off-farm, I will keep the plan steady rather than spread myself too thin. I will put most of my land into cotton because that is my main cash crop and I know how to manage it well. I still want wheat and maize in the plan, because they help me spread risk and keep income from depending on one crop alone. Since I have well irrigation, I will use that to avoid being too passive if spring or summer turns dry. I will not chase the highest possible input level. I will use improved or hybrid seed where it clearly helps yield and stability, but I will keep fertilizer and spray use moderate so costs stay under control. For cotton, I will invest the most attention because it needs more management and gives me the better return. For wheat and maize, I will run a simpler, reliable program with enough fertilizer and water to secure a decent harvest. I will use ploughing on cotton land for a cleaner seedbed and better root growth, and mostly rotary tillage on wheat and maize land to save time and labor.
